subject: MSA + Order Form: rights allocation, training use, and feedback license — next steps
messages:
From: Brightline Procurement <procurement@brightline.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-12T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: MSA redline: training & output ownership concerns

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Our procurement team attached the latest MSA redline (Brightline_MSA_redline_v3.docx) — main asks: Brightline is proposing an explicit assignment of output (Section 5) and a carveout to permit Brightline to use outputs for internal productization. They also want a narrow right to use generated outputs for improving their downstream models (not for training Redwood models).

Two items we need clarified from Redwood before we proceed to legal:
1) Would Redwood accept an output assignment limited to customer-created prompts + outputs (no model weights or derivative retraining of Redwood models)?
2) What evidence/operations attachments can we provide to reassure Brightline that their PII and telemetry will be segregated (they requested an "evidence matrix" in the order form)?

Can you loop in your legal and engineering owners? We are on a tight timeline — procurement hopes to close the order form by 11/18.

Thanks,
Daniel Ruiz
Director, Procurement
Brightline Health

Attachment: Brightline_MSA_redline_v3.docx
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Ruiz <d.ruiz@brightline.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-12T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline: training & output ownership concerns

Daniel — thanks for the clear ask and the redline. Looping in Ben (sales ops), Rishi (legal), and Laura (contracts) to weigh in. High level from product/ops: we can often accept a scoped output assignment but need explicit carveouts to prevent downstream retraining of Redwood-owned models and to preserve telemetry/ops safeguards.

Immediate proposals:
- Output assignment: we are open to assignment/ownership of customer prompts + outputs used solely within Brightline products. This must be limited in the order form Exhibit A with a definition for "Customer Outputs" and an explicit prohibition on using outputs as training data for Redwood model improvements.
- Training/data use: suggest "Use of Customer Data" clause that allows Brightline to use outputs and their own data to train their internal models, but not to transfer or contribute that data to Redwood or any third party without prior written consent. Redwood will retain the operational right to aggregate telemetry statistics for service quality (anonymized, not tied to Customer Outputs).
- Evidence: attaching preliminary RDW evidence matrix (RDW_evidence_matrix.xlsx) — this lists logs we can share, retention windows, and encryption controls. We will need procurement to confirm the exact artifacts they require so we can scope any SOC2/technical attachments.

Rishi/Laura — can you propose exact contract language and flag any procurement asks we should decline (e.g., assignment that conveys model weights, unlimited retraining rights, or sublicensing)?

Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RDW_evidence_matrix.xlsx
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, Daniel Ruiz <d.ruiz@brightline.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline: training & output ownership concerns

Thanks Kim — drafting suggested language inline below and attaching a short redline summary. High-level legal position: we can accept a narrow Customer Outputs assignment but must preserve three protective buckets: (A) no assignment of model weights or internal representations; (B) no right to provide Customer Outputs to third parties for training Redwood models; (C) a notice-and-evidence gating step for any retained telemetry shared beyond Brightline's internal use.

Proposed contract snippets (to include in the Order Form / Exhibit A):
1) "Customer Outputs" defined as: "the textual, visual, or structured outputs generated by the Service in direct response to Customer-provided prompts or queries, excluding model source code, weights, or Redwood internal logs."
2) Assignment scope: "Redwood assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in Customer Outputs, solely for Customer's internal use and productization, provided Customer does not use Customer Outputs to retrain, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any Redwood models or services."
3) Feedback license carve-out: "Customer grants Redwood a limited, nonexclusive, royalty-free license to use deidentified usage telemetry and aggregated metrics for the purpose of operating and improving the Service; Customer Outputs shall not be included in deidentification sets used to train Redwood models absent Customer's prior written consent."
4) Evidence gating: "Before any telemetry or logs that could be re-associated with Customer Outputs are shared beyond operational support, Redwood will provide an evidence package (as defined in the Order Form) and receive Customer's approval; this process will be used for SOC2 or procurement verification purposes only."

Redlines attached: (I will ship as a follow-up short doc). If procurement insists on broader assignment (e.g., sublicensing), we recommend pushing back and offering a limited term license for productization instead.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Brightline Counsel <legal@brightline.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Daniel Ruiz <d.ruiz@brightline.com>, Brightline Procurement <procurement@brightline.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T10:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline: training & output ownership concerns

Kim/Rishi — thanks for the quick turnaround and proposed language. A few clarifications from Brightline counsel:
1) We like the "Customer Outputs" definition but need stronger: can you add "downstream derivatives" explicitly so Brightline can productize features built on the outputs (e.g., UI components, embeddings)?
2) On the feedback license carve-out — Brightline is prepared to accept the "prior written consent" for Redwood to include Customer Outputs in training sets, but requests a defined consent timeline (we propose 10 business days) and a limited exception for anonymized embeddings used for analytics.
3) Evidence gating: Brightline needs a list of exact artifacts (hashes, redaction logs, encryption certs) they will accept; the evidence matrix you sent is a good start but procurement needs concrete proof steps for their security review.

We are aligned on the high-level guardrails. Procurement will escalate to exec signoff if we can't settle these points by COB 11/18.

— Daniel on behalf of Brightline Counsel
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Brightline Counsel <legal@brightline.com>, Daniel Ruiz <d.ruiz@brightline.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T15:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline: training & output ownership concerns — proposed compromise and next steps

Thanks — appreciate the specificity. Quick recap and action items so we don’t miss the 11/18 procurement deadline:

Proposal (compromise position):
- Customer Outputs + "downstream derivatives" can be assigned to Brightline for internal productization; we will clarify examples in Exhibit A.
- Redwood will not use Customer Outputs or downstream derivatives to train or update Redwood models absent explicit written consent.
- Redwood may use anonymized embeddings and aggregate telemetry for service quality; Redwood will exclude any data labeled in the Order Form as "Sensitive Customer Outputs" from analytics without Customer consent.
- Consent process: Redwood will respond to any consent request within 10 business days. If Redwood does not consent, the parties will discuss a short-term pilot license (30–90 days) to allow productization while preserving protections.
- Evidence: We will populate the evidence matrix with concrete artifacts (SSEK/CMS certs, redaction log samples, retention timestamps, sample anonymization hashes). Ben will coordinate with our security team and deliver the updated matrix by EOD 11/17.

Next steps / owners:
- Ben Carter: run security artifact collection and update RDW_evidence_matrix.xlsx (owner: Ben).
- Laura Bennett & Rishi Malhotra: convert the proposal language above into an exhibit/order form redline and share with Brightline counsel (owner: Laura/Rishi) by 11/17 morning.
- Kimberly Park: coordinate exec alignment and confirm procurement timeline with Daniel.

If Brightline agrees to the consent timeline and the evidence artifacts, we can finalize the order form without exec escalation. Please confirm acceptance (or counter) by 11/18 COB.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
